findings_summary: Independent adversarial review of the hygiene role-sector scan fix (compile the six sector regexes once instead of once per line). The reviewer did not read the patch for confirmation but tried to falsify it: it reproduced the pre-patch algorithm verbatim in an out-of-repo harness and compared it against the patched function over 213 generated inputs, obtaining 0 mismatches on the full DetectedArtifact tuple, and measured a ~2800x cost ratio on a 1500-line input. It confirmed the new detection-guard test is not vacuous (RoleMismatch is produced at exactly one site; analyze_hygiene does not dedupe or cap), confirmed the bounded-cost test separates correctly in both directions (old ~26.5 s fails the 2.0 s limit, new ~9 ms passes), and swept all 47 Regex::new sites in the crate to confirm no per-line/per-item regex compilation remains. Nits N1-N3 concern test attribution, the release-only gating of the cost test (an accepted repo convention), and doc-comment style on local consts; none is a behavior change, a defect, or a detection loss.

findings.description: test_role_mismatch_scan_cost_is_bounded times the whole analyze_hygiene pass, so an unrelated future hygiene slowdown would fail it under a role-scan-specific message; by itself it asserts nothing about detection (mitigated by the paired detection guard).

#[cfg_attr(debug_assertions, ignore)] means the cost guard does not run under the standard local gate `cargo test --workspace` (debug); the RED-before property is only observable in --release. Matches the existing documented convention of the sibling R2 cost test.
`///` doc comments on local consts inside the test fn is unusual style; harmless, no warning under clippy --all-targets.

review_chain.note: out-of-repo equivalence harness: 213 cases / 0 mismatches; cost ratio ~2800x; no per-line regex compilation left in the crate; clippy-clean
